status_detail: Private as of 2026-09. A London IPO was prepared for 2026 but City AM (2026-08-12) reports it pushed back to early 2027; TNW (2026-09-09) still calls SumUp a fintech weighing an IPO.
valuation_note: Last priced round: EUR 285M growth round (mostly equity, some debt) led by Sixth Street Growth, 2023-12-11. The exact valuation was not disclosed; the company confirmed an up round above the June 2022 figure of EUR 8B, and CNBC says the round 'values the company north of $8.6 billion'. Reported figure is therefore a FLOOR: EUR 8B x ECB 2023-12-11 rate 1.0757 = $8.606B. For reference, the June 2022 EUR 590M round (half equity, half debt) stated EUR 8B (Gruenderszene 2022-06-23, https://www.businessinsider.de/gruenderszene/fintech/payment-startup-sumup-600-millionen-finanzierung-bewertung-auf-8-milliarden/), = $8.394B at ECB 2022-06-23 rate 1.0493. Post-money not stated as such in either source.
hv_entry_round: No SumUp financing round found. HV's stake came via the SumUp-Payleven merger (share exchange), April 2016; HV's original money went into Payleven's first round (summer 2012).
hv_entry_quote: Past investors are all also coming in behind the merged company as part of the deal. ... Investors include Rocket Internet, Holtzbrinck, NEA, BBVA, Groupon and many more.
consideration_finding: Consideration, most likely (not asked for SumUp, but found). No SumUp financing round names HV/Holtzbrinck (2012 Series A, 2013, 2015 pages checked). HV's money went into Payleven (Rocket Internet's card-reader company): its first round in summer 2012 with NEA and ru-Net (TechCrunch 2012-06-22), which matches HV's site year 2012. SumUp and Payleven merged in April 2016 with SumUp on top, and TechCrunch says 'Past investors are all also coming in behind the merged company as part of the deal' (investors named include Holtzbrinck). So HV most likely holds SumUp shares received for its Payleven stake, not from a SumUp round.
notes: REVIEWER FLAG (possible consideration case): HV/Holtzbrinck never appears in a SumUp round I could load. The Aug 2012 SumUp Series A names b-to-v, Shortcut Ventures, Tengelmann Ventures and Klaus Hommels only (https://techcrunch.com/2012/08/23/make-way-for-another-european-square-sumup-launches-with-20m-in-backing/); the 2013 Groupon/AmEx/BBVA pages and the 2015 funding pages do not name Holtzbrinck. Holtzbrinck Ventures was a Payleven investor: Payleven's first round in summer 2012 (NEA, Holtzbrinck Ventures, ru-Net; https://techcrunch.com/2012/06/22/payleven-a-european-square-from-samwers-rocket-internet-gets-tens-of-millions-funding-from-nea-holzbrinck-ru-net/ and https://techcrunch.com/2013/01/20/payleven-the-samwers-answer-to-square-takes-a-high-single-digit-million-dollar-round-led-by-a-mysterious-new-investor/), and deutsche-startups 2013-05-28 lists Holtzbrinck Ventures among payleven's backers (https://www.deutsche-startups.de/2013/05/28/groupon-american-express-sumup/). HV site year 2012 matches the Payleven entry, not a SumUp round. TechCrunch describes the 2016 deal as a merger in which SumUp took the upper position, so HV most likely got SumUp shares as merger consideration for its Payleven stake. Under the sale-consideration ruling this may not count as membership; Erik to rule. HV Capital's own 2021 Enpal release lists SumUp among HV investments, so HV still claims it. Other valuation data points (not priced rounds): Groupon sold shares in a 2023 secondary at a $4.1B valuation (TechCrunch 2023-12-10); IPO talk of $10B-$15B is not a priced valuation.

status_detail: Acquired by SBI Group (SBI Holdings, Japan). Solaris announced on 2025-03-25 that SBI had passed the BaFin/ECB owner-control procedure, which completes the majority acquisition ('Erwerb der Mehrheitsbeteiligung'). Solaris still operates under its own brand as an SBI subsidiary.
valuation_note: Acquired (SBI majority), so no current valuation; kind set to none for consistency with the other acquired rows. The control round itself, for the reviewer: Series G, EUR 140M, led by SBI Group and Boerse Stuttgart Group, announced 2025-02-03; The Munich Eye (https://themunicheye.com/solariss-valuation-drops-dramatically-9814) says the valuation fell to about EUR 90M (x 1.0274 ECB 2025-02-03 = USD 92.5M; pre- or post-money unclear, a EUR 140M raise into a EUR 90M post-money is odd, so EUR 90M may be pre-money).
